Choice card

.dr-choice · __body · __title · __chev · __head · __desc · components/card.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

I need a service done
  1. 1.dr-choiceThe card, one <a href>: --card at radius 16, padding 16, gap 20 (16 at ≤ 389px). No hover; the ring is keyboard-only, 2.5px --ink.
  2. 2.dr-wellThe picture, this card's own size: 56 × 44 with a 48 × 36 picture box.
  3. 3.dr-choice__titleThe route's name, 17/600, --ink on the card 14.37:1, and the link's accessible name.
  4. 4.dr-choice__chevchevron.forward, 16px --slate, 5.95:1, flush with the trailing edge and aria-hidden.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Choice card.

States

Light

Dark

Try it: hover, press, Tab. Follows the theme switch above.

I need a service done

From role-select.

When to use

A choice card is navigation, not a picker: every instance is a link that leaves the screen. It is the fork at the start of a path. On role-select the user says who they are, and on support they name what went wrong. On the two alert logs it is the row that opens the order an alert is about.

A card a person taps is a title. The title names the destination in the user's words: I need a service done, My order didn't arrive, Safety or trust concern. It takes a description only where the destination is not self-evident from the words. On an alert row that is the proof of which order and when, Package delivery · 10:12. The description sits inside the link, so the title alone carries the purpose (WCAG 2.4.4).

Sources: DESIGN.md § The choice card carries the arrow again · § The choice card's title goes back to the title step's 600 · § The alert log's list row · inventory.md § 1.5 · voice.md P2, P4

Rule and anti-rule

Do

  • My order didn't arrive
  • The photo or report isn't right

support's triage, as the screen builds it: a <ul> of cards, each a different route, and the title is the whole of what the user needs to read to pick one.

Don’t

Instant to card •••• 3318Bank transfer

Choice cards used to set a value on the same screen. A value the form keeps is a radio, or a picker row when the list is long enough to need its own drawer. A choice card always leaves.
